name: c3-watchdog
description: The c3-watchdog panel as an Android app: a WebView showing the REAL dashboard, drawn by c3-watchdog-tui inside nix-on-droid and transcribed to HTML.

build.external_inputs_doc: Artifacts this APK bakes in from ANOTHER repo, so the publish gate can see them. The gate hashes git objects and none of these are in this repo: the panel binary was rebuilt with fixes, this app's own source had not moved, and the gate skipped publishing forever while every rebuild agreed the APK was current.

_doc: The app owns no layout. It asks the terminal for a screen at the grid this device actually has and injects what comes back. Every previous attempt to re-draw that dashboard outside the panel diverged on frames, alignment and colour, so nothing here reproduces any of it.

watchdog._doc: Baked into libs:watchdog as WATCHDOG_TARGETS_JSON_B64 / _CMD. Host, port, user and the command are DATA, never Kotlin constants — the same rule cloud-ide's terminal-targets.json follows. Loopback because Android shares 127.0.0.1 across app sandboxes. Auth is key-based and the key is generated in-app: add the public line (Setup screen) to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys in the env. The app pushes its own panel and sampler into the env's cache at connect time and runs them from there, so a bare nix-on-droid needs nothing installed — only the ssh key, which the env's own installer provisions.

nix-on-droid.label: Nix-on-Droid
nix-on-droid._doc: 8024, read off the device, not the 8022 that was assumed: nix-on-droid's sshd_config sets Port 8024 on this phone. Data, so a phone that differs is a one-line change here.

tools._doc: Where libs:watchdog fetches the binaries it SHIPS. The APK carries them; nothing is ever installed on the phone. aarch64 static musl, because that is every Android device this decade and musl does not care which libc the environment has — or whether it has one.

modules._doc: settings.gradle iterates this (FIRE rule 6: never hardcode the list). `dir` is how a module is SHARED by reference rather than copied: the lib lives once in ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs and every app points at that one directory, so a fix lands in all of them at build time.

libs:web-core._doc: #1371 THE embedded web view: CloudWeb.create(ctx, WebProfile.X), profiles, GPU probe, render-process recovery, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:core._doc: #743 fleet mesh membership. core DEFINES and REQUESTS CONSTELLATION_DATA and carries libs:devtools by `api` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, the MESH_MEMBER package query), so linking it is what makes this app a mesh member every other app can see and reach. Shared BY REFERENCE, like every app's core.

libs:ui-kit._doc: 2026-10-15 owner decision: all apps must be Compose. Shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's Compose kit (CloudKitTheme + KitPalette) MainActivity paints with.

libs:devtools._doc: Not linked by the app module: libs:core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` resolves against THIS settings, so the include must exist or core fails configuration.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:ui-icons._doc: libs:bottomnav's dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:theme-background._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency (the page background); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:perms._doc: #1360/#1352 libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency: Configs ▸ General ▸ Perms is libs:perms' AppPermsSection, first run asks every never-asked grant.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Mirrors aa_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms pins so all the Android projects share one toolchain story. Node is added for the Acode (Cordova) fork's JS/plugin build.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD telling you to use the one shared key — it never generates or substitutes a random/legacy key.
signing._doc_ssh: The ONE declared ssh key every constellation app uses to reach a phone terminal, resolved exactly like the ONE signing key: from the vault, sops-decrypted by build.sh::_resolve_ssh_key, baked to BuildConfig.CLOUD_SSH_KEY_B64, never hardcoded and never generated. The public half is committed in the open at cloud-u-linux/da__my-konsole/termux/authorized_keys, which is what the env provisions — so a phone trusts the key before any app is installed and there is no paste-this-line setup step. NO FALLBACK: a build without the vault fails rather than shipping an app that mints a key the phone has never heard of.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution, the same data-driven block every app here has. build.sh oras-push + gh-release read it; the workflow only invokes those engine commands and hardcodes no registry or tag. This block is ALSO what makes the app discoverable: aa_cloud-superapp/data/regen.sh admits a sibling on .android.application_id + .release.ghcr, so registering in the constellation is a property of the app rather than a list to edit. {sha} -> git short sha, {version_name} -> android.version_name.

ghcr._doc: ENABLED. It was disabled when packages came out private — the cause was the login preferring secrets.GHCR_TOKEN, a PAT, which creates an ACCOUNT-owned package that is born private and cannot be patched. Every workflow here logs in with GITHUB_TOKEN now, which creates the package FOR THE REPOSITORY and takes the repository's visibility; verified on cloud-u-linux, whose first GITHUB_TOKEN push produced a public package. The workflow checks after every push and says so if it ever regresses.

auto_update._doc: The in-app updater reads release_url first (libs:updater Fleet.kt) and only falls back to GHCR, which this app no longer publishes — so updates come off the release asset, which follows repo visibility. NOTE: version_code is 1 and never bumped, so this channel is inert until it is.

gh_release._doc: rolling_tag is canonical: one release the ship workflow overwrites on every main push, so /releases/latest/download/C3-Watchdog.apk is a stable URL.

variants._doc: The same shape ac_cloud-browser and every other per-ABI app declares. Without it both matrix legs uploaded ONE asset name to the rolling release and raced: the second leg's --clobber deleted the first's asset mid-upload, which surfaced as HTTP 404 on the assets endpoint. Worse than the error, the winner was arbitrary — an x86_64 APK could land as C3-Watchdog.apk and be installed on an arm64 phone.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Is everything in the fleet alive? One glance
about.description: Cloud C3 Watchdog is the c3-watchdog panel on the phone: the real dashboard drawn by c3-watchdog-tui inside the Nix terminal and shown as HTML. It answers one question fast — is everything in the fleet that should be running actually alive — with container and service liveness at a glance. It exists so an outage is seen on the phone before a user reports it, and so the same dashboard the owner uses on the desktop is the one on the phone, not a second implementation.
features: The real watchdog dashboard, drawn by c3-watchdog-tui
Runs inside nix-on-droid, shown as HTML
Container and service liveness at a glance
Refreshes on its own while open
Same dashboard as the desktop TUI

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.what: The live watchdog dashboard: every service and its state.

screens.name: Alerts
screens.what: What is down and since when.

guide: Make sure Cloud Terminal Nix is installed: the dashboard is drawn there.
Open the app to see the live dashboard.
Tap a red row to see which service is down and since when.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

related.why: Runs c3-watchdog-tui, which draws this dashboard.
Signs in to the fleet and holds the tokens and secrets this app reads.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
